text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports left foot pain after a soccer injury sustained the previous day.
- history of present illness: while playing soccer, the patient was stepped on and twisted their foot when another player fell onto it, causing immediate pain and removal from play. No prior left foot injury. Managed with elevation, icing, a trainer wrap, and ibuprofen; pain is 3/10 without ibuprofen and 7–8/10 with it.
- physical examination: vitals within normal limits (BP 118/72, HR 58, RR 14, afebrile, SpO2 99% on room air). Heart and lungs normal. Left foot shows bruising on the dorsal and plantar surfaces, swelling, midfoot tenderness, positive piano key test, brisk capillary refill, intact dorsalis pedis pulse, and intact motor and sensation. Imaging shows dorsal displacement of the second metatarsal base, 3 mm separation of the first and second metatarsal bases, and a bony fragment in the Lisfranc joint.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: left foot pain; no numbness or tingling.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: MRI to assess ligament injury; likely surgery (open reduction with plate and screw fixation, same-day discharge); cast, crutches, and no weight-bearing on the left foot for 6–8 weeks, then gradual weight-bearing; clinic follow-up on Monday morning; nurse to start paperwork.
